added_models.model: Vemurafenib-resistant primary human melanoma xenografts (drug addiction, intermittent dosing)

efficacy.model: Vemurafenib-resistant primary human melanoma xenografts (drug addiction, intermittent dosing)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 23302800, epub 2013-01-09). Two primary human melanoma xenograft lines selected to vemurafenib resistance by continuous dosing.
efficacy.note: Vemurafenib-resistant xenografts became drug-dependent; a discontinuous (4-weeks-on/2-off) vemurafenib schedule forestalled lethal resistance. No patient test yet.
efficacy.short: Intermittent dosing forestalls resistance in xenografts
efficacy.quote: We further demonstrate that a discontinuous dosing strategy, which exploits the fitness disadvantage displayed by drug-resistant cells in the absence of the drug, forestalls the onset of lethal drug-resistant disease.
efficacy.judgement: Opened as its own track: a different system (resistant, drug-addicted xenografts) making a different prediction (a schedule prevents resistance) from the V600E-xenograft track. Prospective: S1320 was registered 18 months later to test it.

efficacy.model: Vemurafenib-resistant primary human melanoma xenografts (drug addiction, intermittent dosing)
efficacy.magnitude_basis: post-randomisation median PFS: 9.0 months continuous vs 5.5 months intermittent (105 vs 101 patients)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 33020646, epub 2020-10-05). NCT02196181 first posted 2014-07-21; no results posted on the registry as of 2026-11. P = 0.064 against a pre-specified two-sided alpha of 0.2.

patient_trials.quote: Continuous dosing yielded a statistically significant improvement in post-randomization progression-free survival compared with intermittent dosing (median 9.0 months versus 5.5 months, P = 0.064, pre-specified two-sided α = 0.2).

efficacy.note: SWOG S1320: intermittent dabrafenib+trametinib (3 weeks off, 5 on) shortened post-randomisation PFS, median 5.5 vs 9.0 months continuous; prediction reversed.
efficacy.quote: Therefore, contrary to the initial hypothesis, intermittent dosing did not improve progression-free survival in patients.
efficacy.population: BRAF V600-mutant, non-progressing after an 8-week continuous lead-in
efficacy.judgement: Placed in efficacy, not dose: the model's claim was a schedule-efficacy claim (longer control of resistance), the schedule was delivered exactly as randomised with no exposure target to reach, and the trial's primary endpoint (PFS) is what answered it; a derived dose entry would count the one failure twice. product_in_model false: the model used vemurafenib, the trial dabrafenib (a member) plus trametinib (not a member); both drugs were withheld in the intermittent arm, and the paper attributes the test to the BRAF-inhibitor drug-addiction hypothesis, so the contra is anchored on the class drug. Scored opposite: PFS moved against the prediction, not merely short of it.

efficacy.model: Vemurafenib-resistant primary human melanoma xenografts (drug addiction, intermittent dosing)
efficacy.magnitude_basis: primary endpoint PFS not improved by the intermittent schedule (medians not read)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 34853302). PFS medians not read; the abstract states the primary endpoint of PFS improvement was not met. NCT02583516 first posted 2015-10-22; no results posted.

patient_trials.quote: The trial did not meet its primary endpoint of progression free survival (PFS) improvement.

efficacy.note: Spanish phase 2 (NCT02583516): intermittent vemurafenib+cobimetinib missed its PFS primary; the model's own drug, same answer.
efficacy.short: Vemurafenib intermittent trial also missed PFS
efficacy.quote: Our results show that the antitumor activity of the experimental intermittent schedule of vemurafenib plus cobimetinib is not superior to the standard continuous schedule.
efficacy.judgement: Strengthens the contra with the model's own drug (vemurafenib) in patients; the paper itself sets the preclinical intermittent-dosing rationale against the result. Cobimetinib (non-member) was co-dosed, as in S1320.

efficacy.model: Vemurafenib-resistant primary human melanoma xenografts (drug addiction, intermittent dosing)
efficacy.magnitude_basis: median PFS 8.5 months intermittent vs 10.7 months continuous (HR 1.39); ORR 57% vs 77%
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 38029480, epub 2023-11-24, print Eur J Cancer 2024). 79 patients; PFS HR 1.39 (95% CI 0.79-2.45, p = 0.255), underpowered but same direction as S1320. NCT03352947 first posted 2017-11-24; no results posted.

patient_trials.quote: With 19 months median follow-up, INT was inferior in all efficacy measures: median PFS 8.5 vs 10.7mo (HR 1.39, 95 %CI 0.79-2.45, p = 0.255)

efficacy.note: INTERIM (NCT03352947): intermittent dabrafenib+trametinib inferior on every efficacy measure, median PFS 8.5 vs 10.7 months; composite PFS+QoL primary.
efficacy.quote: INTERIM findings are consistent with other recent clinical trials reporting that intermittent dosing does not improve efficacy of BRAF+MEK inhibitors.
efficacy.reason: Three trials: intermittent dosing never beat continuous
efficacy.judgement: Third randomised test, third miss; the paper states the comparison with the preclinical rationale. Composite primary (PFS and QoL) treated as the primary; both components favoured continuous dosing.

added_models.model: Melanoma patient-derived xenografts matched to the donor patient's BRAF/MEK-inhibitor response

efficacy.model: Melanoma patient-derived xenografts matched to the donor patient's BRAF/MEK-inhibitor response
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read via Europe PMC (PMC4259423). Oncotarget 5(20):9609, 2014.
efficacy.note: Gothenburg melanoma PDX programme: 23 of 26 biopsies engrafted with histology, mutations and expression matching the donor; built to guide treatment.
efficacy.short: Melanoma PDX built to guide treatment
efficacy.quote: Here tumor biopsies from patients with stage III and IV metastatic malignant melanoma were transplanted into immunocompromised mice to generate PDXes.
efficacy.judgement: Opens the patient-level PDX track at its first use; the first comparison is in the same paper.

efficacy.model: Melanoma patient-derived xenografts matched to the donor patient's BRAF/MEK-inhibitor response
efficacy.magnitude_basis: direction of response to BRAF inhibitor, MEK inhibitor and the combination in one patient vs nine PDX
efficacy.confidence_note: Quote is the Figure 3 legend. n = 1 patient, treated in an unnamed BRAF/MEK-inhibitor trial; the PDX arms were run to mimic that trial after the patient's responses were in, so a retrodiction. Patient's own drugs not named in the sentences read.
efficacy.note: Case 2: nine PDX randomised to vemurafenib, trametinib or both reproduced the donor's responses to BRAF inhibitor, MEK inhibitor and combination.
efficacy.short: One patient's PDX matched her responses
efficacy.quote: The responses of Case 2 (patient M120521A) to BRAF inhibitors, MEK inhibitors or both were similar in the patient and the PDX model
efficacy.judgement: Scored retro, not same: the PDX arms were designed to mimic a trial the patient had already been through. Patient-level because the question is whether this patient's tumour responds. PDX dosed with vemurafenib, a member.

efficacy.model: Melanoma patient-derived xenografts matched to the donor patient's BRAF/MEK-inhibitor response
efficacy.magnitude_basis: durability of BRAF-inhibitor benefit: patient PFS 16 weeks vs PDX no response on PLX4720, regression then relapse on combination
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read on PMC (PMC5726788), section 'Predictive Value of PDX for Response to Targeted Therapies'. Partial: the patient had a 70.6% partial response before relapsing at 16 weeks, which the PDX (no response to PLX4720) did not reproduce; the paper counts the early relapse as the prediction. PDX dosed with the tool analogue PLX4720, not vemurafenib.
efficacy.note: Wistar collection (459 PDX): pre-therapy PDX from a patient relapsing on vemurafenib at 16 weeks did not respond to BRAF inhibitor; progressed-patient PDX stayed resistant.
efficacy.short: Pre-therapy PDX reproduced early vemurafenib relapse
efficacy.quote: Tumors did not respond to BRAF inhibition, but regressed on BRAF/MEKi combination followed by relapse
efficacy.population: BRAF V600E melanoma relapsing on vemurafenib (one patient); 47 BRAFi/MEKi-progressed patients
efficacy.judgement: Kept on the one PDX track: same system (melanoma PDX) and same prediction (the donor's response) as Einarsdottir, a different institution. Retro with partial: resistance reproduced, the initial partial response not; a checker could read the missed initial response as contra. The 57 progressed-patient PDX were maintained on BRAFi or BRAFi+MEKi diet matching each patient's therapy and stayed resistant, a second concordance in the same paper.

efficacy.model: Melanoma patient-derived xenografts matched to the donor patient's BRAF/MEK-inhibitor response
efficacy.magnitude_basis: resistant vs sensitive by donor's prior BRAF-inhibitor progression: 4/4 progressed resistant, 3/3 naive sensitive
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read via Europe PMC (PMC7054294; epub 2019-12-20, print Br J Cancer 2020). The patient comparison is made on PDX-derived cultures (PDXC) screened with vemurafenib and cobimetinib; the in-vivo PDX correlated with the cultures (vemurafenib rho = 0.98). Seven matched donors; no trial named.
efficacy.note: Eight BRAF-mutant PDX and their cultures: all four from patients progressed on BRAF inhibitor were vemurafenib-resistant, three treatment-naive responded; PDX vs culture rho 0.98.
efficacy.quote: Overall, PDXCs recapitulate the resistance to BRAF and MEK inhibitor therapy observed in the patient, and PDXCs from treatment-naive BRAF-mutant melanoma patients showed a marked response to BRAF and MEK inhibitor therapy.
efficacy.population: BRAF V600E/K metastatic melanoma, treatment-naive or progressed on BRAF/MEK inhibitors
efficacy.reason: PDX reproduce donors' BRAFi sensitivity/resistance after the fact
efficacy.judgement: Retro: every donor's BRAF-inhibitor outcome was known before the PDX/PDXC were screened. No prospective, PDX-guided treatment decision for a member drug has been reported, so the track never leaves retro.

added_models.model: Novartis PDX clinical trial (PCT): ~1,000 PDXs, one mouse per model per treatment, population response rate

efficacy.model: Novartis PDX clinical trial (PCT): ~1,000 PDXs, one mouse per model per treatment, population response rate
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 26479923, epub 2015-10-19); body paywalled (nature.com served references only). The abstract names no drug; the BRAF-mutant melanoma encorafenib arm is described in the authors' 2018 commentary.
efficacy.note: Novartis ran population-level 'PDX clinical trials' (62 treatments, six indications), including encorafenib alone and with binimetinib in BRAF-mutant melanoma PDX.
efficacy.short: Novartis PDX clinical trial includes encorafenib
efficacy.quote: We demonstrate both the reproducibility and the clinical translatability of this approach by identifying associations between a genotype and drug response, and established mechanisms of resistance.
efficacy.judgement: Own track: a population-level PDX screen (one mouse per model) giving a class response rate, distinct from the donor-matched PDX track (patient level) and from cell-line xenografts. Encorafenib, a member, was dosed (product_in_model true).

efficacy.model: Novartis PDX clinical trial (PCT): ~1,000 PDXs, one mouse per model per treatment, population response rate
efficacy.magnitude_basis: objective response rate: ~65% of BRAF-mutant melanoma PDX on encorafenib vs 53% (vemurafenib, BRIM-2) and 59% (dabrafenib, BREAK-2) in patients
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read on PMC (PMC5821416), Mol Cell Oncol 5(2), epub 2018-02-09 (Crossref). Gao 2015's paywalled body cites the same trials (Sosman 2012, BREAK-2) and likely states this comparison first, which would move the date to 2015; not verified. Patient comparators' response rates (53%, 59%) taken from the cited trials, not re-read here.
efficacy.note: Authors set the PCT encorafenib response (~65%, BRAF-mutant; 0 NRAS-mutant responders) beside vemurafenib and dabrafenib clinical response rates; BRAF+MEK raised PDX response to 100%.
efficacy.short: PCT encorafenib response matched clinic rates
efficacy.quote: the BRAF inhibitor encorafenib demonstrated an approximately 65% response rate among BRAF-mutant melanomas, which is consistent with the response rates reported for vemurafenib and dabrefinib in the clinic.
efficacy.judgement: Retro: the vemurafenib (2011-12) and dabrafenib (2012-13) response rates were public before the 2015 PCT, so the match is a reproduction of known results. Class level: the comparison is a population response rate. No prospective comparison with encorafenib's own patient response rate (COLUMBUS, PFS primary) was stated, so none is scored.

considered_not_added: Encorafenib 13-week rat skin findings (hyperkeratosis, scabbed/flaking skin, paw swelling) in sources/210496/210496Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.txt, reconciled by the reviewer with clinical skin toxicity: same rat-and-dog toxicology system as the draft's rat-dog-toxicology track, so it is a new 2018 entry on that existing track (same for hyperkeratosis, track stays contra on vemurafenib's cuSCC), not a new model; outside this file's scope.
FDA pharmacology review NDA 202429 executive-summary dog paw 'wart-like growth': a missed fact on the existing rat-dog-toxicology track (note fix, hedged n = 1), not a new system.

Krepler 2016 Clin Cancer Res (12 PDX from BRAF-inhibitor-progressed patients, 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-15-1762): same melanoma-PDX system as the added track; its abstract uses the PDX to find second-line combinations and does not state a PDX-vs-donor response comparison, and the author manuscript was not served, so no quotable entry; cited in the 2017 entry's note.

Dabrafenib's and encorafenib's own BRAF V600E cell-line and xenograft packages (A375, Colo205 and similar): the same system as the draft's braf-v600e-cell-xenograft track, skipped per the same-system rule.

PDX-derived cultures (PDXC) in Ice 2019: an ex-vivo readout of the same PDX, folded into the PDX track rather than opened as a separate ex_vivo system because the paper validates PDXC against the PDX, not independently against patients.

Braf V600E/Pten-null (Tyr::CreER) genetically engineered mouse melanoma: Europe PMC search returned no paper stating a comparison of a member drug's effect in the GEMM with patient results; no patient comparison found.
Zebrafish BRAF V600E melanoma: no paper comparing a member drug's zebrafish effect with clinical response; no patient comparison found.

Melanoma ex-vivo organoids / short-term cultures for members: search returned only an immune-organoid feasibility study and a glioma series; no stated comparison with clinical response to a member drug.

In-silico models: encorafenib food/PPI PBPK (Mol Pharm 2023) is an absorption model, not a dose-selecting disease model compared with patients; the BRAF-MEK-ERK ODE model (npj Syst Biol 2024) has no patient comparison. Not added.
IMPemBra (NCT02625337; short-term dabrafenib+trametinib added to pembrolizumab): tests immunotherapy priming, not the drug-addiction schedule prediction; not a test of this track.
